sections.h2: Which Orange County offices handle my property tax?
sections.html:
Three offices split the work in Orange County, and each answers a different question. The Property Appraiser sets the value and approves exemptions, local taxing bodies set the millage rate, and the Tax Collector mails the bill and takes payment.

  • Property Appraiser: ownership record, mailing address, legal description, assessed value and exemptions such as homestead
  • Taxing authorities: the county commission, the school board, cities and other levying bodies set the rate per $1,000 of taxable value
  • Tax Collector: bills, payments, installment plans, delinquent taxes and tax certificates

The Tax Collector's page says it distributes revenue to 63 taxing authorities in the county. Non-ad valorem items such as streetlights, sewage and road work appear on the same bill but are charged per unit, not by value.

sections.h2: When are Orange County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bills go out by November 1, and the full amount is due by March 31. Anything unpaid on April 1 is delinquent.

Orange County property tax calendar (Orange County Tax Collector and Florida Department of Revenue)
WhenWhat happens
January 1Value is set as of this date
March 1Deadline to file exemptions with the Property Appraiser
AugustNotice of Proposed Property Taxes mailed
November 1Tax bills mailed by this date
November to FebruaryDiscounts of 4, 3, 2 and 1 percent
March 31Full amount due, and homestead deferral applications due
April 1Unpaid taxes delinquent
On or before June 1Tax certificate sale

The Tax Collector states that a payment counts as late if it arrives after March 31, whatever the postmark says.

sections.h2: How do early payment discounts work in Orange County?
sections.html:
The discount falls by one point each month: 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February. March carries no discount.

A homeowner who sells in the winter often pays the whole bill at closing, so the month of closing changes what the bill costs. Ask your title agent or the Tax Collector which figure applies on your closing date. If a mortgage company pays your taxes from escrow, it may request the bill, and you then receive a copy marked as requested by the lender. That copy is not a second demand for payment.

Owners with a prior-year bill above $100 who are current on taxes may apply for the quarterly installment plan, filed online with the Tax Collector.

sections.h2: What exemptions can reduce an Orange County tax bill?
sections.html:
Homestead is the main one. The Property Appraiser says it can cut the taxable value of a qualifying home by up to $50,000, and the Department of Revenue explains that the first $25,000 applies to all taxes while the second layer reaches only non-school taxes on value above $50,000.

You apply to the Property Appraiser by March 1, and the home must be your permanent residence on January 1. The state also describes widow, disability, senior and military exemptions, and it says the Save Our Homes cap limits annual assessment growth on a homestead to the lower of 3 percent or inflation. A sale resets the property to just value on the next January 1, so a buyer's bill can run higher than the seller's. The Property Appraiser offers a tax estimator meant for people planning to buy or sell.

sections.h2: What happens if taxes are unpaid when I sell in Orange County?
sections.html:
Open balances have to be cleared by the time the deed changes hands, and the title agent will request the exact figure from the Tax Collector. After April 1, the Tax Collector adds a 3 percent minimum charge and advertising cost to delinquent real estate taxes.

Parcels are advertised once a week for three weeks, and the certificate sale follows on or before June 1. Bids open at 18 percent and fall. To redeem, the owner pays the delinquent tax, interest and advertising cost. After the delinquency date the Tax Collector takes only certified or cashier's checks, money orders, certain attorney, title or escrow checks, or cash in person, and it does not take personal or business checks.

  • Order a payoff from the Tax Collector before listing
  • Check escrow records if a lender pays the bill
  • Confirm that no certificate has been sold on the parcel

sections.h2: What if a certificate goes two years without payment?
sections.html:
A certificate holder may then file for a tax deed, and Orange County runs those sales through the Comptroller's Office. The holder cannot contact the owner to demand payment during the first two years, which state law sets.

Homestead property gets an extra layer of protection at the opening bid: state law adds one-half of the latest assessed value to the amounts due. A seller in this position should act early, since a tax deed sale ends with the owner losing the house and the closing window is short. Call the Tax Collector's property tax department for a redemption figure.

sections.h2: What about rental property and tangible personal property tax?
sections.html:
Landlords face a second tax. The Tax Collector explains that tangible personal property tax is an ad valorem tax on furniture, fixtures and equipment in businesses and rental property, and it also reaches structural additions to mobile homes.

Those bills arrive with the real estate bills and earn the same early-payment discounts, and they go delinquent on April 1 like the rest. Interest then runs at 1.5 percent per month, plus advertising and fees, and a collection agency under contract with the Tax Collector adds a 15 percent fee if the account is not paid in full. If you sell a rented home with furnishings, ask the Tax Collector how an open tangible account is handled before closing.

sections.h2: How does the Homestead Tax Deferral work?
sections.html:
It lets a qualifying homesteader postpone part of the tax, and the application is due to the Tax Collector by March 31. The program is not the same as the exemption, which is filed with the Property Appraiser.

Deferred tax stays a lien on the home. That makes it relevant to anyone selling, so ask the Tax Collector how a deferred balance and its interest are paid off at closing. State rules cap the deferral by household income, and a permanent resident aged 65 or older may defer the part above 3 percent of household income.

sections.h2: What does the county look like for owners?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists 1,528,002 people as of July 2025 living in 527,776 households. Over half of those homes are owner lived, valued at a middle figure of $390,100, while carrying owners pay a median $2,055 a month and renters a median $1,775.

A bill's mix of taxing districts depends on where the home sits, whether inside a city or in unincorporated Orange County, so read the district lines on your own bill.

faqs.q: When is the Orange County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: March 31. Bills are mailed by November 1, and unpaid taxes become delinquent on April 1. The Tax Collector counts receipt, not postmark.

faqs.q: How much is the early payment discount in Orange County?
faqs.a: It runs from 4 percent in November down to 1 percent in February. Nothing is taken off in March, when the gross amount is due.

faqs.q: Which Orange County office fixes a wrong value or missing exemption?
faqs.a: The Orange County Property Appraiser. The Tax Collector cannot change a value, an owner record or an exemption, and only collects what the certified roll says.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Orange County house if I owe back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance, interest and charges can be cleared at the closing table. Request the Tax Collector's payoff first, and plan on certified funds if the bill has already gone delinquent.

faqs.q: Does a tax certificate mean I lost my house in Orange County?
faqs.a: No. A certificate is a lien, not a deed. The owner can redeem by paying the taxes, interest and advertising cost, and only after two years can the holder apply for a tax deed.
